subject: Dedicated capacity: Polaris Health - KV cache & quantization sizing
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@polarishealth.ai>, Tom Whitman <t.whitman@polarishealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity kickoff + model details request

Hi Leah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we want to size a Reserved (Dedicated) pool that will reliably serve your clinical summarization pipeline with predictable latency during peak hours. To give a concrete quote and set of recommendations we need a couple of model-specific datapoints from your side:

- Model family + parameter count (e.g., inst/alpha-30B or internal-144B)
- Typical max context length for production (and % of requests at that length)
- Expected concurrency (qps) and P95 latency SLO (both for 512-token and 2,048-token contexts)
- Whether KV cache persistence between requests is required (session stickiness)
- Any constraint around quantization (cannot quantize above X, or must keep float16 for regulatory reasons)

I’ve looped in Karthik and Marcus from our infra/planning team to produce an ops-oriented sizing once we have those numbers. I also attached an initial spreadsheet template (polaris-kv-scenarios.xlsx) you can fill — feel free to drop it back or point us at the internal doc.

Goal: provide a recommended reserved pool config (GPU type, instance count), expected monthly reserved cost, and fallback routing strategy if capacity is exceeded.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@polarishealth.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Whitman <t.whitman@polarishealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickoff + model details request

Hi Hannah —

Thanks — quick answers inline and attached a filled copy of the spreadsheet: see polaris-kv-scenarios.xlsx.

- Model: internal clinical-30B (decoder-only, optimized from an LLM baseline). We can't share weights but the architecture mirrors a 30B parameter MHA-style model with hidden dim ~4096.
- Max context: we run up to 6,144 tokens for long-case summaries, but ~60% of traffic is <= 1,024 tokens and 15% hits the 4k-6k range.
- Concurrency: baseline peak concurrent requests ~60 qps, bursting to 110 qps during morning triage windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency target 250ms for 512 tokens; for 2k contexts they expect p95 under 850ms.
- KV cache: session stickiness is desired (patient sessions), but full persistence across days not required. We prefer to keep embeddings/KV cache warm for active sessions.
- Quantization: security team is OK with int8 for weights but insists activations/KV cache remain FP16 for now (policy reason).

Also adding Tom (platform) in case infra constraints change. Happy to jump on a technical call if you want more telemetry.

-Leah
Leah O'Connor
Head of AI Platforms, Polaris Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@polarishealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickoff + model details request

Team —

Leah's info is very helpful. A few clarifying technical points before Marcus and I lock in numbers:

1) KV cache sizing assumptions: Leah says activations/KV must remain FP16. For a 30B-class model with hidden_dim ~4096 and 32 attention heads, a conservative estimate for KV memory is: ~2 * hidden_dim * 2 bytes * sequence_length per token (keys + values stored in FP16). That simplifies to ~16KB/token (order-of-magnitude) for their architecture.
   - For 6,144 tokens that implies ~96MB of KV per concurrent request (this seems low — need to double-check multiplication).

2) Param memory: with int8 weights (we can host quantized kernels) + FP16 activations/KV, we should estimate parameter resident memory of ~15–18GB for a 30B model (weights quantized to int8 on disk, dequantized in runtime as needed / or served via int8 kernels).

3) Inference overhead (work buffers, logits, optimizer not used): assume an additional ~4–8GB per model instance depending on batch size and sequence length.

4) Multi-model packing: can we collocate multiple smaller models on a single GPU? For now Polaris is single-model (clinical-30B).

Action: Marcus, can you produce a few sizing scenarios (p95 targets met) for:
  A) conservative (no batching, low latency)
  B) mixed (auto-batching, some KV cache sharing for sessions)
  C) cost-optimized (aggressive batching, lower concurrency guarantees)

I'll also validate the per-token KV math; I want to ensure we don't undercount for 6k contexts.

-karthik

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@polarishealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickoff + model details request — sizing scenarios and numbers

Folks —

I ran three scenarios in the attached spreadsheet and pasted the most relevant numbers below. I used conservative multipliers to account for runtime buffers and larger attention-state memory at long context lengths. Note: numbers assume NVIDIA H100-style 80GB GPU (could be adjusted down if Polaris is willing to accept slower p95 with 60GB A-series alternatives).

Assumptions/factors used:
- Model param resident (quantized int8): 16GB (includes small dequantization workspace).
- FP16 activations + KV per token: 2 * hidden_dim * 2 bytes ≈ 32KB/token for our compiled kernel assumptions (this is conservative for their transformer config).
- Additional runtime overhead: 6GB per model instance.

Per-request KV footprint (conservative):
- 1,024 tokens -> 32KB * 1,024 ≈ 32MB
- 2,048 tokens -> 32KB * 2,048 ≈ 64MB
- 6,144 tokens -> 32KB * 6,144 ≈ 192MB

Memory per concurrent request (model params + KV + overhead):
- baseline instance resident: 16GB params + 6GB overhead = 22GB (shared if collocated).
- For each concurrent request that needs a dedicated model copy (no model sharding): add KV per request.

Sizing scenarios (target p95 latencies as requested):
A) Conservative (low-latency, minimal batching)
   - Target throughput: 60 qps steady, 110 qps bursts
   - Approach: dedicate a model instance per ~4 concurrent requests to avoid contention (small async batching disabled)
   - Effective per-GPU concurrency (H100 80GB): ~3 model instances per GPU (3 x 22GB = 66GB, leaves ~14GB headroom)
   - Concurrent requests supported per GPU (assuming 4 reqs per instance): 12 qps concurrently at short contexts (512-1k); ~6–8 for long 4k–6k contexts due to KV memory pressure
   - GPUs required for steady 60 qps: ~6–7 H100s; for 110 qps burst: ~10–12 H100s (we recommend burst pool + autoscaling)

B) Mixed (auto-batching and session KV warm cache) — recommended starting point
   - Use intelligent batching with max batch size 8 and reuse KV cache for active sessions. This reduces per-request wall-clock but requires scheduler complexity.
   - Effective per-GPU concurrency: ~18–24 depending on batching efficiency for short contexts
   - GPUs required: steady 60 qps -> 3–4 H100s; peak 110 qps -> 6–7 H100s

C) Cost-optimized (aggressive batching, higher latency tolerance)
   - Assume p95 targets relaxed by ~2x; leverage larger batch sizes and kernel fusion.
   - GPUs required for 60–110 qps: 2–5 H100s (highly dependent on batching efficiency and acceptable latency windows)

Quantization impact notes:
- Weight quantization to int8 lowers resident param size to ~16GB from ~32–34GB FP16; this enables more model instances per GPU but offers limited reduction in KV/activation memory because those must remain FP16 per Polaris policy.
- Because KV must stay FP16, long-context workloads (4k–6k) still drive memory; savings are primarily in model storage, not per-token cache.

Operational recommendations:
1) Start with the Mixed scenario (B) with 4 H100 reserved + 4 H100 burst pool. This meets p95 goals while keeping committed cost reasonable.
2) Enable session-aware KV caching with a TTL (e.g., 2 hours) so active patient sessions remain warm. This reduces repeated cold KV costs and cuts backend QPS by ~12–18% in our sim.
3) Instrument token-level telemetry and run a 7‑day production-like load test before final commit.
4) If Polaris later approves KV/int8 or int4 caching, we can shrink reserve further.

I attached the detailed per-GPU worksheet (polaris-kv-scenarios.xlsx) and a simple reserved-pool topology (reserved-pool-map.png).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickoff + model details request — sizing scenarios and next steps

Leah / Tom —

Really helpful — thanks for the quick turn. Next steps I propose:

1) Polaris reviews Marcus' spreadsheet and confirms whether we should move forward with the Mixed scenario (4 reserved H100 + 4 burst).
2) Book a 60-minute runbook + load-test window (Rohan will own test execution).
3) Sign the reserved capacity SOW (I’ve attached a draft NDA and SOW link but will send formal DocuSign once scope confirmed).

Leah — can you confirm by EOD Monday whether Polaris is comfortable with the Mixed starting point? If yes we’ll schedule the load test and lock pricing for the first 3 months.

Best,
Hannah

Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
